brief: Goldman's Molavi frames a market that came into the week 1% from all time highs without feeling like it. Iran and US re-escalation took oil above $100 and up 7% on the week, August payrolls printed 162k against estimates by over 100k with June and July revised up, Waller was dovish and Hammack hawkish, so good news reads as bad news and CPI later sets the Fed tone. The central argument is a yield spiral: AI capex funding moved from cash to cash, debt and equity, AI related borrowing ramped as yields rose rather than slowing, big tech issuance is tracking close to $250bn or around 70% of Treasury issuance into a converging buyer base, while $10 trillion of debt approaches refinancing and Bessent's over $5bn of buybacks has not worked. Leadership rotated from semis to software and cybersecurity, IGV up about 6% against SOXX down about 2.2% over the past month, which he calls the cleanest active call and a pain trade. Investors stay long but less gross than May and June, hedged for duration and hikes and rotating defensive. Seasonals turn as buybacks and retail slow. Return profile skews negative.
